name: Star number
definition: The **star number** $\mathrm S(\mathcal H)$ is the largest $|S|$ for which some $S\subseteq\mathcal X$ and $T\subseteq S$ satisfy $$T\in\mathcal H_{|S}\quad\text{and}\quad T\mathbin{\triangle}\{x\}\in\mathcal H_{|S}\quad\text{for every }x\in S.$$
graph_summary: The largest number of one-coordinate neighbours of a realized centre, over all projections.
origin_references: Introduced as the combinatorial measure called the star number in \cite{hanneke2015minimax}.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

monotonic.proof: Every star contained in a subfamily remains a star in the containing class.

p_monotonic.proof: A star in a projection is realized by the original class on its star coordinates.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{001,010,011,100,101,110\}$ has Star Number 2. Conditioning its last coordinate to 0 or 1, and deleting that coordinate, gives respectively $\{01,10,11\}$ and $\{00,01,10\}$; each is a 2-star. Thus $\mathrm S(\mathcal H)$ is not strictly larger than the smaller fibre value.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: Tight strict c-monotonicity requires strict c-monotonicity, which is refuted by the displayed six-concept class.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Strict monotonicity requires strict c-monotonicity, which fails for the displayed six-concept class.
